This is the Food Line briefing for June 5, 2026.

13abc reported that Toledo food pantries were preparing for increased demand as SNAP benefits faced a shutdown pause.

When benefits are delayed or paused, food pantries may see higher demand from households that rely on SNAP.

Source: 13abc.

Where: Toledo.

Date: June 5, 2026.

What happened: 13abc reported rising food-assistance demand across its service area in Toledo, affecting SNAP households.

Who may be affected: SNAP households

Why it matters: When benefits are delayed or paused, food pantries may see higher demand from households that rely on SNAP.

Read the source: https://www.13abc.com/2025/10/28/local-food-pantries-are-preparing-increased-demand-snap-benefits-face-shutdown-pause/

USDA set to cut $1B for food programs. WA food banks are worried from Cascade PBS.

Why it is included: This report provides background on local food-assistance conditions that help explain today’s lead story.

What the source says: Local banks are already struggling to meet demand, and federal cuts could mean empty shelves for the 1 in 4 Washingtonians who visited one last year.

Read the source: https://www.cascadepbs.org/politics/2025/04/usda-set-cut-1b-food-programs-wa-food-banks-are-worried

The government shutdown is now in its 4th week and food banks across Texas are working hard to keep up with rising demand. from KLTV.

Why it is included: This report provides background on local food-assistance conditions that help explain today’s lead story.

What the source says: Michael Close, Chief Operating Officer at Swan Food Pantry, has seen a 17% increase the past three weeks in people asking for food assistance.

Read the source: https://www.kltv.com/2025/10/29/food-pantries-struggle-keep-up-with-rising-demand-due-government-shutdown-snap-benefits-delays
